system.name: CRAB
system.one_liner: a control loop that lets users steer their own Internet path performance by reallocating, reclaiming, or probing bandwidth across their flows

content.subject: CRAB's control loop: which of four priority-ordered actions to take after each throughput measurement

elements.name: Wait & Measure
elements.role: central hub state that measures throughput and picks the next action; redrawn both in the outer loop and inside Bandwidth Probing

elements.name: Reclamation
elements.role: highest-priority action: reclaim bandwidth a growing flow had lent out to others

elements.name: Reallocation
elements.role: second-priority action: lend bandwidth unused by non-saturating flows to saturating flows

elements.name: Decrease Bandwidth Estimate
elements.role: third-priority action: lower the total bandwidth estimate and redivide it between flows by weight

elements.name: Bandwidth Probing
elements.role: default, lowest-priority compound action taken when no other condition holds; a nested sub-loop that probes for more bandwidth

elements.name: increase a saturating flow f's assigned rate by inc
elements.role: entry action of Bandwidth Probing: bumps one saturating flow's rate by the probe step inc

elements.name: Redivide new bandwidth estimate between flows, double the value of inc
elements.role: taken when the probe increased observed throughput; grows the probe step for the next round

elements.name: Reset flow f's rate and inc's value
elements.role: taken when the probe did not increase throughput; undoes the rate bump and exits probing

relations.what: any flow growing (drawn both from the outer state and from within Bandwidth Probing)
at least one non-saturating and one saturating flow exist
observed throughput dropped and no saturating flow exists
returns to measurement after decreasing the estimate

relations.to: increase a saturating flow f's assigned rate by inc
relations.what: none of the above applies; enters Bandwidth Probing (no numbered badge)

relations.from: increase a saturating flow f's assigned rate by inc

relations.to: Redivide new bandwidth estimate between flows, double the value of inc
Reset flow f's rate and inc's value

relations.from: Reset flow f's rate and inc's value
relations.what: returns to the outer measurement, exiting Bandwidth Probing

steps.what: if any flow is growing, reclaim bandwidth it had lent out
else if at least one non-saturating and one saturating flow exist, lend unused bandwidth to saturating flows
else if throughput dropped and no flow is saturating, decrease the bandwidth estimate and redivide it by weight

transitions.guard: at least one non-saturating and one saturating flow exist
throughput dropped and no saturating flow

decisions.question: which action does CRAB take after a throughput measurement?
branches: one non-saturating & one saturating flow -> Reallocation
throughput dropped, no saturating flow -> Decrease Bandwidth Estimate

decisions.question: inside Bandwidth Probing, did the rate increase help?
branches: throughput increased -> redivide and double inc
throughput did not increase -> reset rate and inc

content.key_idea: CRAB's control loop is a strict priority order over four actions - reclaim, reallocate, decrease, or probe - always returning to a shared measurement state before checking again.
content.reading_order: starts at 'Wait & Measure', follows the numbered guarded arrows 1, 2, 3 out to Reclamation, Reallocation and Decrease Bandwidth Estimate, and otherwise descends into Bandwidth Probing

palette.used_for: medium-blue fill of the outer action states (Reclamation, Reallocation, Decrease Bandwidth Estimate) and the Bandwidth Probing container
gray fill of the three inner Bandwidth Probing action boxes
pale-blue fill of the 'Wait & Measure' ovals

style.stroke: thin black outlines on all boxes and ovals
style.arrows: thin black arrows, mostly straight with some curved returns; each forward transition carries a black circular numbered badge beside its guard-condition text
style.font: sans (Arial), small bold italic state-name labels with smaller condition text

encoding.color_means: blue marks the outer priority-ordered action states and the Bandwidth Probing container; gray marks the three inner probing actions; pale blue marks the shared 'Wait & Measure' state wherever it recurs
encoding.line_style_means: not used to distinguish transitions; solid arrows throughout, curved for returns and cross-cutting exits, straight for direct causes
encoding.state_means: each action is its own coloured box; the same 'Wait & Measure' state is redrawn at two places (outer loop and inside Bandwidth Probing) rather than distinguished by colour
encoding.marker_means: circled numbers 1-3 rank the priority order in which guard conditions are checked, reused with locally analogous guards inside the nested Bandwidth Probing sub-loop
encoding.emphasis: the large blue Bandwidth Probing container visually demotes the fourth, unlabelled default action to a subordinate sub-diagram, matching its place as the last-checked, catch-all branch
reusable_patterns: a central hub state with priority-numbered guarded transitions fanning out to peer action states, all returning to the hub
a compound state drawn as a large container holding its own miniature copy of the hub-and-spoke pattern
weaknesses: the 'Redivide new bandwidth estimate...' box has no drawn outgoing arrow, so the figure alone does not show how the probing loop continues after that action
reusing the same three numbered badges for two different sets of guard conditions (outer vs. inner) could be misread as one shared priority order

evidence: we take one of the four actions in the exact priority order
If there exists any growing flow, we do reclamation for it
We return to the throughput measurement after each action.

summary: This figure is a simplified state diagram for CRAB's control loop, a rate-allocation policy that runs after every throughput measurement. From the central 'Wait & Measure' state, three numbered, guarded transitions check conditions in strict priority order: (1) if any flow is growing, go to Reclamation; (2) else if both a non-saturating and a saturating flow exist, go to Reallocation; (3) else if throughput dropped with no saturating flow, go to Decrease Bandwidth Estimate. If none apply, control instead falls into Bandwidth Probing, a nested compound state that increases one flow's rate, re-measures, and then either doubles its step size when throughput improved or resets the rate when it did not, reusing the same three-way priority check before exiting back to the outer 'Wait & Measure'. Every action eventually returns control to that shared measurement state.
summary_zh: 该图为CRAB控制环状态图：以Wait & Measure为中心，按优先级①②③转向Reclamation、Reallocation或降速；否则进入Bandwidth Probing子循环调速，最终都返回测量态。
notes: Kept prior groups ['logic','walkthrough'] since the numbered badges give a priority order, though they are not a single trace through a structure drawn once; 'steps' lists only the 3 badges that literally appear (there is no 4th badge for the default Bandwidth Probing branch). 'Wait & Measure' is drawn twice (outer loop and inside Bandwidth Probing) but modelled as one element since the text describes a single recurring state. No source-SVG colour histogram exists for this figure, so palette hex values come from the index's measured-attributes summary. The 'Redivide...' box has no drawn outgoing arrow in the figure; this is left as a noted gap rather than invented.
